name: metamorphosis

phase_0.boundary_condition: the chitinous exoskeleton and hormonal threshold

VINIT.justification: the unexpressed genetic potential before cellular differentiation begins

TANCH.justification: the final biological limit that contains the reproductive cycle

AFWD.justification: the constructive metabolic process driving growth toward the next stage

AREV.justification: the enzymatic breakdown of larval tissues into a fluid state

CLINK.justification: the sequential shedding of old skin to allow for expanded form

IMSCRIB.justification: the internal cellular clusters that retain the blueprint of the final form throughout dissolution

FSPLIT.justification: the divergence of the organism into histolytic breakdown and histogenic reconstruction

FFUSE.justification: the emergence where the dissolved matter and the new structures reunite as a single organism

EVALT.justification: the successful formation of adult structures from undifferentiated cells

EVALF.justification: the suspension of development or failure to progress due to environmental stress

ENGAGR.justification: the transitional state where larval behavior ceases but adult morphology is not yet visible

IFIX.justification: the irreversible hardening of the new cuticle after emergence

phase_3.void_description: the pre-embryonic state where no morphological structure exists
phase_3.true_description: the successful attainment of the reproductive imago stage
phase_3.false_description: developmental arrest or metabolic failure within the pupa
phase_3.both_description: the chrysalis interior where the organism is simultaneously liquid and structured

steps.domain_action: the zygote establishes the initial genetic state
the larva consumes nutrients to increase biomass
the organism undergoes multiple larval instars
imaginal discs identify themselves within the larval body
the final larval instar records its maximum weight
the pupal stage initiates the divergence of tissue states
histolysis dissolves the larval digestive and muscular systems
diapause holds the system in a state of metabolic stasis
histogenesis utilizes the dissolved nutrients to build wings and legs
the organism exists as a non-functional soup containing functional blueprints
eclosion integrates the new organs with the remaining biological systems
the imago recognizes its completed morphology
the wings expand and harden permanently
the reproductive adult reaches the terminal boundary of the life cycle

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the endocrine system translating environmental cues into hormonal pulses
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: juvenile hormone and ecdysone concentrations in the hemolymph
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the epigenetic markers and DNA sequences within the imaginal discs
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: photoperiod and temperature sensors regulating the timing of molts
phase_5.alfs_store: the species-specific genome stored in every cell nucleus

phase_6.cycle_cost: metabolic energy stored as lipids and glycogen
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: larval biomass with high potential energy
phase_6.post_cycle_state: imago morphology with high structural complexity and reduced energy reserves
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the increase in structural order is balanced by the heat of metabolic dissolution
